newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK money rates steady to easier in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: HK money rates steady to easier in moderate trade.

text.p: Interbank rates were steady to easier in moderate trading on Friday, with activities focusing on short-date money, dealers said.
The overnight rate eased slighty to 4-7/8 3/4 at midday from 4-15/16 7/8 percent on Thursday. Three-month money was little changed at 5-5/8 1/2 percent.

"Short-term money eased slightly as offerings increased after bank borrowing for the preparation for an initial public offering of a stock early in the morning pushed overnights to a high of about 5-1/2 percent," a local bank dealer said.
The market was liquid with limited interest in term money, dealers said. Trading in government paper was relatively quiet with some traders already having closed their books ahead of the year-end.

"For the preparation of the Real Time Gross Settlement system, banks need to hold certain amount of bills and notes. Otherwise, December is traditionally a very quiet month for government issues," one dealer said.
One-week bills yielded 4.11 percent, up from 4.09 on Thursday. One-month yields were unchanged at 4.30 percent.
Three-year note yields edged up to 6.15 percent from 6.14, the seven-year yield rose one basis point to 7.13 percent and the longest 10-year note yielded 7.37 percent versus 7.34.
